watchpoint.semantics: MAME 0.281 installs a pre-commit write tap (points.cpp:231-237); debug_watchpoint::triggered sets wpaddr/wpdata and runs the action before the write commits (points.cpp:314-355). old=b@wpaddr is the pre-write byte; new=wpdata is the value about to be written; stop5cd0.bin is the independent after-state.
watchpoint.pc_semantics: M6809 read_opcode_arg increments PC during operand fetch (m6809.h:202); tap PC is post-fetch for PSHS. Stack pushes write low byte before high byte (m6809.lst PUSH_REGISTERS). BSR/JSR tap PC is the return address they push. Hardware IRQ stacking saves the interrupted PC and the full register set (base6x09.lst IRQ).
watchpoint.auxiliary_note: The printf field labelled st10 is w@(s+10); MAME parses 10 as hexadecimal, so it is the word at S+0x10, not S+0x0A. The IRQ resume PC is therefore taken from the watched 0797/0798 frame word, not from st10.

irq_frame_0790_0798.kind: 6809 hardware IRQ frame push (entire state), not PSHS/JSR
irq_frame_0790_0798.frame_bytes: 0790..0798 watched: DP=00 X=80A6 Y=FC4F U=0672 PC=716A; B/A/CC at 078F/078E/078D are outside this watchpoint and are taken from the event registers B=27 A=47 CC=C0 plus the unchanged stop snapshot

final_0799.semantics: M6809 PSHS pushes B; value written is B=02, not a return address

final_079a_079b.semantics: BSR pushes its own return address 715F (low byte 5F first, then high byte 71)

final_079c_079d.semantics: PSHS A,B pushes B first then A; 079D=B=02, 079C=A=91

final_079e_079f.semantics: JSR pushes its return address 5A0A; 079E=5A unchanged, 079F 05->0A

outer_fe70.note: s0x10 is the word at S+0x10 because MAME parses the expression literal 10 as hex; the IRQ resume PC is the watched frame word 0797/0798=716A
